title: Japanese and Korean shipbuilders deploy robots to take on China
source_used: Hokanews relaying the Financial Times (via Coin Bureau); FT original blocked (403)
key_facts: South Korean and Japanese shipbuilders are speeding up the use of robots in their yards to cope with labour shortages, ageing workforces and rising costs, and to compete with China (FT, as relayed).
Chinese shipyards took 63% of global ship orders last year.
HD Hyundai has introduced robots for routine welding and is targeting partially 'dark' (largely unmanned) factories by 2030.
Hanwha Ocean says one worker can supervise up to 10 robots and aims to automate 70% of its manufacturing processes.
Japan's Fanuc, a robot maker, wants shipyards eventually to run as many robots as people, including more overnight operation.
quote_evidence: South Korean shipbuilder HD Hyundai has already introduced robots to perform routine welding tasks, according to the report. Hanwha Ocean has also expanded its use of robotics, saying that one worker can supervise as many as 10 robots.
Chinese shipyards secured 63% of global ship orders last year
why_it_matters_hint: Heavy industry in two ageing countries is turning to robots to stay in the race with China's shipyards.
notes: FT paywalled/blocked. Facts come from Hokanews, a low-tier site, which itself credits the FT via Coin Bureau; figures are consistent with public company targets but not independently checked here. Tracking code removed from the FT url.
